name: Fasted cardio
lead: Fasted cardio is aerobic exercise performed after an overnight fast, typically first thing in the morning before eating. It is a staple of bodybuilding-style cutting phases, where practitioners believe that exercising with low carbohydrate stores increases the share of energy drawn from body fat.

The practice is discussed in physique and looksmaxxing circles as a way to lean out for a defined look. The sources available for this entry are thin: no trial of fasted versus fed cardio was reviewed, and the only published material in the research set is a case report of bodybuilders' contest-preparation habits.

paras: In bodybuilding, competitors generally gain muscle in an off-season and then cut, eating below maintenance and adding cardiovascular exercise to lose fat before a contest.[1] Fasted cardio is a variant in which the cardio session is done before any food that day.

A 2017 case report and critical review interviewed six competitive bodybuilders and their coaches about the nutrition, drug and training strategies they used, and compared them with scientific evidence. The report documented high anabolic-steroid use among the participants and examined their diet and training in bulking and cutting phases.[2] The authors' conclusions on fasted cardio specifically are not available in the text reviewed here.

No studies found in the sources reviewed for this entry that directly compare fasted with fed cardio. The only related research located is a descriptive case report of six bodybuilders' practices, which is not a controlled test of the method.[2]

refs.title: Nutrition, Pharmacological and Training Strategies Adopted by Six Bodybuilders: Case Report and Critical Review

card.summary: Morning cardio before eating, a bodybuilding cutting habit with little direct research in the sources reviewed.
card.note: No controlled comparison of fasted and fed cardio was found in the sources reviewed.

quick.overview:
Fasted cardio means doing aerobic exercise before the day's first meal. It is common in bodybuilding cuts.

The sources reviewed contain no controlled trial comparing it with fed cardio, so claims about added fat loss are untested here.
quick.mechanism: Proponents say low carbohydrate availability after an overnight fast shifts fuel use toward fat during the session.
quick.risks: No harms were documented in the sources reviewed. The one related paper is a case report on bodybuilders whose routines also included heavy anabolic steroid use.
